revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Party Plans
revealWordProblem.text: Reginald is having hot dogs at his party, and 24 people are coming. His mom wants the same number of hot dogs and buns, with none left over. Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns come in packs of 8. How many packs of each should they buy, and how many hot dogs and buns will they have?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A pack of hot dogs labeled 10 count beside a pack of hot dog buns labeled 8 count.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: To buy matching numbers with no unmatched hot dogs or buns, find a common multiple of the pack sizes. Multiples of 10 are 10, 20, 30, 40, …; multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, …. The least common multiple is 40, so buy 4 packs of hot dogs and 5 packs of buns for 40 matched servings. This supplies at least one serving for each of 24 guests. If each guest eats exactly one, 40 − 24 = 16 matched servings remain. Thus 'none left over' can mean no unmatched hot dogs or buns; exactly 24 servings with no leftovers is impossible using only these whole packs.

iDo.title: Example · GCF or LCM?
lines: Hot dogs come in packs of 10. Buns come in packs of 8. You want the same number of hot dogs and buns. What is the least number of each you can buy?
Decide: GCF or LCM?: packs → multiples → LCM
Find the least common multiple: LCM = 40
Find how many packs of each: 40 ÷ 10 = 4; 40 ÷ 8 = 5
Buy 40 of each: 4 packs of hot dogs and 5 packs of buns.
linesEs: Las salchichas vienen en paquetes de 10. Los panes vienen en paquetes de 8. Quieres el mismo número de salchichas y de panes. ¿Cuál es el menor número de cada uno que puedes comprar?

Haz una lista de múltiplos de 10 y de 8: 10, 20, 30, 40; 8, 16, 24, 32, 40
Halla el mínimo común múltiplo: mcm = 40
Halla cuántos paquetes de cada uno: 40 ÷ 10 = 4; 40 ÷ 8 = 5
Compra 40 de cada uno: 4 paquetes de salchichas y 5 paquetes de panes.

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: Use prime factors to find the GCF of 48 and 36. Then explain why the method works.
Write 48 and 36 as products of primes. (48: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 → 36: 2 × 2 × 3 × 3)
Multiply the primes both numbers share. (2 × 2 × 3 = 12)
Why do we multiply only the primes both numbers share? (A common factor must divide both numbers. Only the shared primes are in both 48 and 36.)
linesEs: Usa factores primos para hallar el MCD de 48 y 36. Luego explica por qué funciona el método.
Escribe 48 y 36 como productos de primos. (48: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 → 36: 2 × 2 × 3 × 3)
Multiplica los primos que comparten los dos números. (2 × 2 × 3 = 12)
¿Por qué multiplicamos solo los primos que comparten los dos números? (Un factor común debe dividir a los dos números. Solo los primos compartidos están en 48 y en 36.)

extending.stem: Claim: “The GCF of two numbers is always smaller than both of them.” Always, sometimes, or never true?
choices: Always — a common factor has to be smaller than what it divides
Sometimes — it equals the smaller number whenever that number divides the larger one
Never — the GCF is always one of the two numbers
Sometimes — it depends whether the numbers are even
extending.explanation: The GCF can never be larger than the smaller number. But it can equal it, when the smaller number divides the larger one exactly. Check 6 and 18: 6 divides 18, so the GCF is 6. That one example makes the claim sometimes true.
choiceFeedback: A number is a factor of itself. Try 6 and 18.
The GCF of 10 and 15 is 5, which is neither of them.

extending.stemEs: Afirmación: “El MCD de dos números siempre es menor que los dos.” ¿Siempre, a veces o nunca es cierto?
choicesEs: Siempre — un factor común tiene que ser menor que lo que divide
A veces — es igual al número menor siempre que ese número divida al mayor
Nunca — el MCD siempre es uno de los dos números
A veces — depende de si los números son pares
extending.explanationEs: El MCD nunca puede ser mayor que el número menor. Pero puede igualarlo, cuando el número menor divide exactamente al mayor. Comprueba 6 y 18: 6 divide a 18, así que el MCD es 6. Ese único ejemplo hace que la afirmación sea a veces verdadera.
hintsEs: Busca un par donde un número divida al otro exactamente.
